note: The two sets are nearly identical claim-for-claim; the only substantive difference is that A states the W8X10 a second time as 'member | section | W8X10' while B states it as 'structural member | section profile | W8X10', a marginally less vague but equally redundant restatement. Both bind the same values to the same members, both attach 'TYP' as a condition to lengths and sections when the drawing's '1/4" TYP' applies to the 1/4" dimension, and both treat the reference keynote '05 12 23.A7' as a specification of the HSS 4 X 4 X 1/4. Both repeat C3X6 and W8X10 several times under different entity names and both leave out W10X15 and numerous dimensions. With identical strengths and identical errors, neither set is meaningfully better.
remarks: The text layer is a spatially scrambled list of dimension strings and member labels, so most dimension-to-component bindings (e.g. 'C3X6 | length | 1'-4"', 'C3X6 | dimension | 10"', the bare '4"', '6"', '8"' claims) cannot be verified from the text alone and are effectively unbound fragments. 'TYP' is repeatedly misused as a condition on lengths/sections although the sheet only shows '1/4" TYP'. Both sets omit W10X15 (a distinct member shown on the sheet), HSS4X4X1/4 as a member, and many dimensions (1'-3", 11 1/2", 5 7/8", 1 13/16", 5 1/8", 1 3/8", 5/8", 6 7/8", 2", 1") plus the detail scales 1 1/2" = 1'-0". Quotes such as 'W10X12 TYP' and 'C3X6 10"' are assembled from non-contiguous text-layer tokens and do not support the claims as written.
